task: generic pure-u64 Rust counter from one natural-language instruction
instruction: Build a pure local Rust counter transition. Increasing it by a requested unsigned 64-bit amount must add exactly that amount when the sum fits; otherwise keep all state unchanged. It must never decrease or wrap. Propose a precise mathematical contract for my review, then implement it and independently verify the accepted contract. Keep all data local.

execution.environment: shared CPU workstation; includes developer-harness review

host_review: explicit isolated developer-harness semantic rejection, not a user approval or an NL/formula equivalence theorem

proposed_contract.name: counter_transition
proposed_contract.description: A pure Rust counter transition that increases the counter by a requested amount when it fits, otherwise keeps the state unchanged. It must never decrease or wrap.
proposed_contract.specification: { counter := if s.counter + increment > s.counter then s.counter + increment else s.counter }
assumptions: All values are non-negative unsigned 64-bit integers
The counter state is always valid
The increment parameter is always non-negative

review_rejection: Isolated developer-harness semantic review: rejected. Nat addition never wraps. At s.counter=18446744073709551615 and increment=1, this specification returns 18446744073709551616, whereas the requested transition must retain the original state. The example 100+1000 ->100 also contradicts the requested behavior and this formula, since 1100 fits u64. No implementation/formula repair supplied.
